body.objective: Add a simple resident-worker await/wakeup protocol so a long-lived Codex- or Claude-like research stream that blocks or exhausts its queue can notice newly READY work without a human having to type into its terminal.
body.stop_condition: Land and document an initial operational primitive such as `s-f work await --stream S --agent A --timeout D` that watches the append-only programme state without busy polling, returns immediately when one pullable item exists, and emits a compact human line plus versioned byte-stable JSON containing the exact item ID, effective state, queue order, programme revision and reason it is pullable. The first version may stop before acquiring a lease, but it must compose safely with `s-f work pull`; an optional `--pull --expires T -o brief.md` mode may atomically acquire only after the item becomes pullable. Provide stable exit codes for READY, timeout, interrupted, malformed history and lease conflict; preserve terminal-title updates using the stream and agent identities; expose a file/socket notification suitable for a future TUI or resident supervisor; and document the recommended agent loop: report or block current work, release the lease, await, then pull exactly one successor. Include deterministic fixtures for ready-at-start, work arriving after an event append, unrelated-stream traffic, queue-order change, timeout, signal cancellation, malformed event, expired lease, another resident winning the race, and a stream that changes from all-BLOCKED to READY. Demonstrate bounded CPU and filesystem activity over a fifteen-minute idle interval.
body.forbid: no attachment to, keystroke injection into or prompt scraping from arbitrary running AI processes; no automatic scientific work generation; no lease acquisition before a concrete item is pullable; no unbounded lease; no broad git mutation; no busy loop; no treating PROPOSED work with unmet dependencies as READY; no bypass of one-exclusive-lease discipline; no hidden wall-clock dependence in deterministic tests; no terminal title that collapses all workers to `s-f coordinator` or the repository name; no claim that process wakeup means scientific progress
notes: Observed failure on 2026-07-20: Quantum correctly blocked two items and released both leases, the coordinator added a new READY matter-anomaly item, but the resident process remained idle because it had already ended its turn and had no queue-change notification.
The immediate need is deliberately smaller than persistent AI-session RPC: provide a safe await primitive and a documented resident loop first.
This should integrate with the queue-forecasting and fast-overview work later, but it is independently useful and should not wait for statistical forecasting.

Second live reproduction, 2026-07-20: Black Hole closed `black-hole-symplectic-extension-normal-form` at 14:23:56Z, explicitly stated that it would pull `black-hole-symbolic-cross-invariant` next, and then remained at an idle prompt for more than ten minutes while the authoritative queue contained three READY items. No lease conflict or missing dependency existed. This is exactly the report/release/await/pull gap the requested primitive should close without prompt scraping or keystroke injection.

Third live reproduction, 2026-07-21: at 23:56:14Z the coordinator used `s-f work assign` to establish bounded live leases for black-hole-1, nonlinear-1 and quantum-qme-1 on three independently READY items. Ten minutes later the programme contained only the coordinator-authored ACQUIRE/ACTIVE events and no worker report or scientific-file modification in any of those three allowed-path sets. This absence does not prove that a model is not reasoning, but it proves the operational point: lease assignment itself provides no resident notification, acknowledgement or liveness evidence. The await/wakeup primitive should therefore emit an explicit resident acknowledgement/heartbeat after delivery while preserving the rule that a heartbeat is not scientific progress.

Fourth live reproduction at the complete 2026-07-21T00:34:20Z coordinator fold: black-hole-1, nonlinear-1 and quantum-qme-1 still held the coordinator-assigned leases acquired at 23:56:14Z, Classical held its lease from 00:16:17Z, Bridge and Observer held their earlier leases, and every lease remained formally LIVE with valid successors. Nevertheless there was still no resident-authored WORK_REPORTED/transition event or modification in any active scientific allowed-path set during the preceding twenty minutes. Do not infer process death or release leases from this advisory absence; instead use it as acceptance evidence that assign/lease is not delivery. The production workflow needs a resident-side await subscription and explicit acknowledgement whose event identifies stream, agent, item and programme revision, while remaining separately typed from scientific progress.
